title: Multiple Conditions (and/or)
story: The sign at the roller coaster says: "Must be at least 130 cm tall AND at least 10 years old." You're tall enough, but are you old enough? A single comparison won't cut it � you need to check TWO things at once!
why: Real-world decisions almost always involve multiple conditions � combining them with AND/OR lets programs make smarter, more realistic choices.
analogy: && is like a door that needs TWO keys to open. || is like a door that opens with EITHER key.
try_it: Check if a number is between 10 and 20 (greater than 10 AND less than 20). Then check if a number is less than 5 OR greater than 95. Change the number and watch the result flip!
tips: `&&` is stricter than `||` � AND needs everything true, OR just needs one thing true
You can chain more than two: `a && b && c` means all three must be true
Use parentheses to group: `(age >= 13 || has_permission) && height >= 120`
common_mistakes: Writing `and` or `or` as words instead of `&&` and `||` � XIOM uses the symbols!
Forgetting that both sides must be complete comparisons: write `x > 5 && x < 10`, not `x > 5 && < 10`
